Report Description
THE SHERBURNE COUINTY PLANT WILL BE RELEASING APPROXIMATELY 3000 POUNDS OF AMMONIA (NH3) TO THE AIR BETWEEN 10 AM AND 10 PM ON SATURDAY JUNE 2ND. THIS IS A PLANNED RELEASE FROM THE UNIT 1 BOILER VENT VALVES WHICH ARE LOCATED 250 FEET ABOVE THE GROUND AT AN ELEVATION OF APPROXIMATELY 1200 FEET ABOVE SEA LEVEL. THE SOURCE OF THE AMMONIA IS A BOILER CHEMICAL CLEANING SOLUTION CONTAINING APPROXIMATELY 7.5% AMMONIA. DURING THE PASSIVATION STAGE IN BOILER CLEANING OXYGEN IS INJECTED INTO THE SYSTEM TO REACT WITH SURFACE METALS TO GENERATE A CORROSION RESISTANT SURFACE. A BYPRODUCT OF THE PROCESS IS THE VAPORIZATION OF AMMONIA FROM SOLUTION, AND ITS EMISSION TO THE AIR. BOILER CLEANING WITH THIS CHEMICAL SOLUTION IS A COMMON PROCESS USED BY UTILITIES THROUGHOUT THE UNITED STATES.
